reasons: Compliant classification is supported by the cited text: Section 3.1(a) (p0248) grants an exclusive, worldwide, all-uses licence with no 'revocable' or at-will revocation language, so the walk-away scenario is not present.

Affiliate and contractor coverage sits at the preferred position — Section 3.4(a) (p0255) permits performance through Affiliates without consent, 3.4(b) (p0256) allows multi-tier sublicensing, and 3.4(c)(i) (p0257) allows subcontracting to Third Parties as Sanofi deems appropriate.
Transferability to a successor is expressly satisfied by Section 15.2(a)(ii) (p0611), which permits assignment without consent on a sale of substantially all related assets, merger or acquisition.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed, and both deterministic checks (affiliate coverage, no at-will revocation) pass.

The noted frictions (Affiliate/contractor rights located in Section 3.4 rather than the grant clause; consent for a U.S. 'substantially all' sublicence subject to a reasonableness standard) are minor sub-elements properly recorded in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations.
